reuse.why: The API and existing schedule consumers share the amount calculation and reuse getApproxNumberThreshold, but several callers retain missing-amount dispatch outside the shared definition.

duplication.why: Range and approximate calculations are centralized, although three callers repeat the missing-amount fallback already provided by getScheduledAmount.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules, tolerance remains in shared/rules, and API serialization stays in api-models.

scope.why: The edits are focused on expected schedule amounts, their consumers, supporting tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared calculation improves ownership, but overlapping helpers with different null handling, an optional operator omitted by existing consumers, and stale policy comments make the contract harder to maintain.

bypasses_abstraction.where: updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule in server/schedules/app.ts, plus computeSchedulePreviewTransactions in shared/schedules.ts, retain local missing-amount dispatch instead of using getScheduledAmount's complete fallback.

disguised_duplication.where: The remaining missing-amount checks are explicit; range and approximate arithmetic are shared rather than reshaped into copies.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter and delegates to getExpectedAmount, which adds an isapprox branch; three callers bypass the wrapper's missing-amount handling with local guards.
